learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Normal Awake Background.
Apply Normal Awake Background to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: A normal adult awake EEG usually shows an organised posterior dominant rhythm with appropriate anterior–posterior gradient and reactivity.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Normal varies with age, state and medication. Interpretation integrates frequency, amplitude, symmetry, synchrony and continuity rather than one band value.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Provides the baseline against which slowing, asymmetry and epileptiform activity are judged.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: A normal variant can look unusual when isolated from age and state.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Normal Awake Background?
options: A normal adult awake EEG usually shows an organised posterior dominant rhythm with appropriate anterior–posterior gradient and reactivity.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: A normal adult awake EEG usually shows an organised posterior dominant rhythm with appropriate anterior–posterior gradient and reactivity.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Normal Awake Background?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Normal Awake Background?
options: A normal variant can look unusual when isolated from age and state.
quizBank.explanation: A normal variant can look unusual when isolated from age and state.

reviewPrompts.answer: Normal varies with age, state and medication. Interpretation integrates frequency, amplitude, symmetry, synchrony and continuity rather than one band value.
Provides the baseline against which slowing, asymmetry and epileptiform activity are judged.
A normal variant can look unusual when isolated from age and state.
Organisation often matters more than whether one frequency is “high.”
